result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md in full and apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts line by line against it. This is the highest-stakes gate so far (S7 atomic capacity is a genuine race property) so I did not trust BACKEND-DEV's 20/20 report and independently re-derived AC1 with my own fixtures at higher stress. 1. TRANSACTION/LOCK SHAPE VERIFIED BY READING: registerForEvent (registration.ts:109-216) opens exactly one db.transaction, and EVERY read that participates in the outcome decision -- the events row via .for("update") (line 129), the existing-registration check (line 137-141), and the admitted-count query (line 145-148) -- executes against `tx`, inside that one transaction span, before the pure decideRegistrationOutcome call. Nothing reads via `db` directly inside the writing path. The lock is per-event-row (WHERE id = eventId), not global, matching design §1.1's stated no-cross-event-bottleneck claim. 2. MY OWN CONCURRENCY VERIFICATION (independent of BACKEND-DEV's 20/20, not just re-reading it). Used the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432). Wrote and ran my own throwaway apps/bot/src/domain/registration.reviewer-scratch.test.ts (deleted after use, git status confirmed clean, not part of this commit): a. 50 iterations (up from BACKEND-DEV's 20) of 2 concurrent registerForEvent calls, capacity=1, fresh fixtures per iteration -> 50/50 exactly one admitted + one waitlisted, zero over-admissions, direct DB check confirmed exactly 1 admitted row every time. b. Tighter race: 5 concurrent callers against capacity=2, 20 iterations -> every iteration produced exactly 2 admitted + 3 waitlisted, never more than 2 admitted rows in the DB. c. Direct lock-primitive proof, independent of registerForEvent's own code: opened two raw pg connections, tx1 took `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the events row then `pg_sleep(0.8)` before COMMIT, tx2 issued its own concurrent `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` against the same row -- tx2's query did not resolve until >=750ms had elapsed (measured 800ms+), proving the underlying Postgres primitive this design relies on genuinely blocks a second waiter rather than interleaving. All 3 scratch tests passed. Combined with re-running BACKEND-DEV's own committed 20-iteration AC1 test (still 20/20), I have re-derived the atomicity property under real contention myself, at higher stress than the committed suite alone, not just trusted the self-report. 3. AC2-AC7 INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: read registration.db.test.ts's AC2 (double-registration, exactly one row, current status shown), AC4 (closed/cancelled/finished each refuse before capacity/invite/approval are even considered), AC5 (source='linkedin' from pending_source, cleared to NULL after use -- confirmed both the write and the clear are asserted), AC6 (requires_invite/requires_approval refuse before the capacity branch -- confirmed row order 5,6 before row 7 in decideRegistrationOutcome, and unit-tested in registration.test.ts rows 5/6), AC7 (exactly one audit_log row per admitted AND per waitlisted write, zero for every refusal outcome -- explicit test for the zero case too). All match the design's first-match-wins table (§2.2) exactly, same order, no drift. 4. qr_token / S4: `git grep -n "Math.random" apps/bot/src` returns nothing that touches token generation (only a comment in registration.ts stating the negative constraint). generateQrToken is `randomBytes(32).toString("hex")` -- 256 bits, CSPRNG, no counter, no hash of userId, well clear of S4's >=128-bit floor. It is the only place a token is produced anywhere in the diff. 5. source/pending_source integration (REQ-016 reuse): resolveRegistrationSource/clearPendingSource read/verified against event.ts's existing setPendingSource/getPendingSource shape. clearPendingSource is called only when pendingSource was non-null (registration.ts:197-199), inside the same tx as the insert -- confirmed by the AC5 DB test that pending_source is NULL after a registration consumes it, and that a second unrelated registration without a fresh pending_source falls back to 'direct' rather than reusing a stale value (no cross-registration leakage possible since the column is cleared in the same transaction that consumed it). 6. requires_invite/requires_approval ordering: confirmed rows 5-6 run strictly before row 7 (capacity) in decideRegistrationOutcome (registration.ts:64-72) -- a requires_invite=true event with seats available still refuses, never admits. Matches AC6 and the design's explicit ordering rationale (§2.2). 7. Audit rows: registerForEvent writes exactly one writeAuditLog call (line 201-208), reached only from inside step 8's writing branch, with action keyed off outcome.kind (registration.admit / registration.waitlist) -- exactly one row per insert, on both outcomes, none on any refusal path. This matches the design's own S8 reading (§6) that AC7 does not literally test the waitlist branch but S8's broader "every status change" wording covers it -- I agree with this reading; flagging it for SECURITY-REVIEWER per the design's own §9.4 open question is correct and mandatory (S8 applies). 8. Domain logic outside handlers (decisions/0004): handlers/registration.ts contains no admission-state, capacity, or lock logic -- it only resolves the acting user, calls registerForEvent, and maps outcome.kind to catalog strings via a plain switch (presentation, not a domain rule). No grammY import in registration.ts (domain file). Confirmed clean. 9. Design-system: bot has no UI/CSS surface (confirmed unchanged from REQ-016/018/019 precedent) -- no token/spacing findings apply. i18n additions (types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts) are three-file-parity complete, events.cardCta removed from all three per REQ-020 §7.3's atomic-removal instruction -- confirmed by diff. 10. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT: npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only). npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean. npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root, scratch Postgres up) -> 15 files / 172 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failures. 11. Docker/workspace check: this diff adds no new npm workspace and does not move/rename any build output directory -- no scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. Two MINOR findings (neither blocks this gate -- no AC/security-invariant violation, code-quality/consistency only): - registerForEvent reimplements countAdmittedRegistrations's exact query inline (registration.ts:144-149) instead of calling the reused function the design explicitly names at §1.1 step 3 / §3.2 step 4 (`countAdmittedRegistrations(tx, eventId)`). I diffed the inline query against event.ts's countAdmittedRegistrations (lines 451-460): identical select/where/`.length` shape, so this is not a correctness bug, but it duplicates logic the design said to reuse and the import list (registration.ts:6) omits countAdmittedRegistrations entirely. - handlers/registration.ts:93-95 calls `await getVenueById(db, event.venueId)` for every admitted/waitlisted/already-registered outcome but discards the result -- it is never incorporated into composeRegistrationReply's output. Design §7.2's table states the confirmedPrefix message sources venue name from getVenueById; the shipped reply text never includes it. This is dead code plus an unnecessary DB round-trip on every registration reply, not a functional defect (no AC requires venue name in the message text). Vitest-parallelism finding: BACKEND-DEV's flagged intermittent-failure-under-default-parallelism report is the exact same symptom already tracked as ISS-0014 (docs/issues/ISS-0014.yaml, discovered_by SECURITY-REVIEWER in WF02-REQ-019, status: open, recommends --no-file-parallelism or per-file DB isolation). I am not filing a new issue -- this is a re-observation of an already-open issue, not a new one, and REQ-020's own run confirms `--no-file-parallelism` continues to be the correct mitigation (172/172 clean). No action needed beyond confirming ISS-0014 still accurately describes the gap.

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- atomic capacity independently re-verified at 50 iterations (2-way) + 20 iterations (5-way, capacity=2) + a direct raw-SQL proof that SELECT...FOR UPDATE genuinely blocks a concurrent waiter (>=750ms measured block). Zero over-admissions across all of it.
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- double registration returns already-registered with current status, exactly one row for (event,user), verified by db test.
ac_results.AC3: PASS -- generateQrToken uses node:crypto randomBytes(32) hex-encoded (256 bits), no Math.random/counter/hash-of-userId anywhere in the diff.
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- closed/cancelled/finished each refuse with a stated reason + event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming onward path, verified by db test and handler reply table.
ac_results.AC5: PASS -- source='linkedin' from pending_source, pending_source cleared to NULL after consumption within the same transaction, verified by db test.
ac_results.AC6: PASS -- requires_invite/requires_approval refuse before the capacity branch (rows 5-6 before row 7), verified by unit test and db test.
ac_results.AC7: PASS -- exactly one audit_log row per admitted and per waitlisted write, zero for every refusal outcome, verified by db test including the explicit zero-row case.

issues.description: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts:144-149 reimplements countAdmittedRegistrations's exact query inline (same select/where/.length shape as event.ts:451-460) instead of importing and calling the existing reused function the design explicitly names at REQ-020.md §1.1 step 3 and §3.2 step 4. Not a correctness bug (verified functionally identical), but a duplication the design said to avoid. Recommend BACKEND-DEV replace the inline query with a call to countAdmittedRegistrations(tx, eventId) in a follow-up.

apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts:93-95 calls getVenueById(db, event.venueId) on every admitted/waitlisted/already-registered outcome but discards the result -- it is never used in composeRegistrationReply's output, even though REQ-020.md §7.2's table states the confirmedPrefix message sources venue name from this call. Dead code plus an unnecessary DB round-trip on the hot registration path. Recommend either wiring the venue name into the confirmed-reply text (matching the design) or deleting the discarded call, in a follow-up.

BACKEND-DEV flagged (step-02-backend-dev.json) that default-parallelism vitest intermittently fails/deadlocks with two DB-backed test files sharing tables, recommending --no-file-parallelism become a hard requirement. This is the identical symptom already tracked as ISS-0014 (discovered_by SECURITY-REVIEWER, WF02-REQ-019, status: open) -- not a new issue. Confirmed --no-file-parallelism continues to produce a clean 172/172 for this run. No new issue filed; ISS-0014 remains the correct tracking record.

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory, S4/S7/S8 all apply. In particular, confirm the design's own §9.4 open question: writing an audit_log row on BOTH admitted and waitlisted outcomes (not admitted alone) is the correct reading of S8's broader "every status change" wording versus AC7's literal admission-only text.
